designers.name: Michael Thonet
designers.whyTheyMatter: Turned a chair into a kit of six parts that could be shipped flat and assembled anywhere — mass production before the word existed.

designers.name: Eileen Gray
designers.whyTheyMatter: Worked outside every movement of her time and was written out of the histories until late in her life.

designers.name: Marianne Brandt
designers.whyTheyMatter: Ran the Bauhaus metal workshop and designed for actual manufacture, which most of the school did not.

designers.name: Raymond Loewy
designers.whyTheyMatter: Invented the industrial design consultancy as a business, and the idea that styling sells.
designers.searchQuery: Raymond Loewy Industrial design design work

designers.name: Charlotte Perriand
designers.whyTheyMatter: Built the furniture the Corbusier office is famous for, and spent decades after it doing better work alone.

designers.name: Aino Aalto
designers.whyTheyMatter: Half of the Aalto practice and the one whose glassware is still in production and still cheap.

designers.name: Henry Dreyfuss
designers.whyTheyMatter: Put the human body at the centre of the method and wrote down the measurements everyone still uses.
designers.searchQuery: Henry Dreyfuss Industrial design design work

designers.name: Belle Kogan
designers.whyTheyMatter: One of the first women to run an industrial design office in America, at a time when the profession was closed to them.
designers.searchQuery: Belle Kogan Industrial design design work

designers.name: Gio Ponti
designers.whyTheyMatter: Made a chair light enough to lift with one finger and edited Domus for decades alongside it.

designers.name: Eva Zeisel
designers.whyTheyMatter: Worked in curves when the field was committed to the grid, and kept working into her nineties.

designers.name: Jean Prouvé
designers.whyTheyMatter: A metalworker first and a designer second, which is why his structures show you exactly how they carry load.

designers.name: Clara Porset
designers.whyTheyMatter: Took a vernacular Mexican chair seriously as a modern object, and argued for design rooted in place.

designers.name: Lina Bo Bardi
designers.whyTheyMatter: Left Italy for Brazil and built work that belonged there rather than importing European modernism wholesale.
designers.searchQuery: Lina Bo Bardi Furniture design work

designers.name: Greta Magnusson Grossman
designers.whyTheyMatter: Ran a shop, a practice and a teaching career in two countries, and her lamps still look like next year.
designers.searchQuery: Greta Magnusson Grossman Lighting design work

designers.name: Kaare Klint
designers.whyTheyMatter: Measured furniture and the things people put in it, and turned that into the Danish teaching method.

designers.name: Florence Knoll
designers.whyTheyMatter: Designed the modern office as a system, and commissioned most of the century's famous chairs.

designers.name: Ray and Charles Eames
designers.whyTheyMatter: Treated a chair, a film and a toy as the same problem, and showed their process rather than hiding it.
designers.searchQuery: Ray and Charles Eames Furniture design work

designers.name: Isamu Noguchi
designers.whyTheyMatter: Moved between sculpture and product without deciding which one he was doing.

designers.name: Sori Yanagi
designers.whyTheyMatter: Worked by making models with his hands rather than drawing, and said so.

designers.name: Hans Wegner
designers.whyTheyMatter: Made about five hundred chairs and understood joinery better than anyone who has made fewer.

designers.name: Arne Jacobsen
designers.whyTheyMatter: Designed the building and then everything inside it down to the cutlery.

designers.name: Nanna Ditzel
designers.whyTheyMatter: Kept experimenting with materials for fifty years while her contemporaries settled into teak.

designers.name: Kenji Ekuan
designers.whyTheyMatter: Designed an object so ordinary you have used it without ever looking at it.
designers.searchQuery: Kenji Ekuan Industrial design design work

designers.name: Eliot Noyes
designers.whyTheyMatter: Built the idea that a company should look and behave like one thing, and ran it at IBM for twenty years.
designers.searchQuery: Eliot Noyes Industrial design design work

designers.name: Sergio Rodrigues
designers.whyTheyMatter: Made Brazilian modern furniture out of heavy timber and leather rather than imported slenderness.

designers.name: Dieter Rams
designers.whyTheyMatter: Wrote the ten principles everyone quotes and, more usefully, spent forty years actually following them.
designers.searchQuery: Dieter Rams Industrial design design work

designers.name: Achille Castiglioni
designers.whyTheyMatter: Started from a found object and an argument, and the joke is always structural rather than applied.

designers.name: Marco Zanuso
designers.whyTheyMatter: Worked out how to make furniture from foam and plastic when nobody knew how those materials behaved.

designers.name: Richard Sapper
designers.whyTheyMatter: Built objects that hide their mechanism completely until you need it.
designers.searchQuery: Richard Sapper Industrial design design work

designers.name: Verner Panton
designers.whyTheyMatter: Chased the single-material, single-piece chair for years before the plastics could do it.

designers.name: Anna Castelli Ferrieri
designers.whyTheyMatter: Ran Kartell's design direction and made moulded plastic into something you would keep.
designers.searchQuery: Anna Castelli Ferrieri Furniture design work

designers.name: Gae Aulenti
designers.whyTheyMatter: Worked at every scale from a lamp to a railway station converted into a museum.

designers.name: Ettore Sottsass
designers.whyTheyMatter: Used colour and pattern as arguments about what objects are for, not as decoration.
designers.searchQuery: Ettore Sottsass Industrial design design work

designers.name: Reiko Tanabe
designers.whyTheyMatter: A three-piece plywood stool that has stayed in production for decades on the strength of its geometry.

designers.name: Enzo Mari
designers.whyTheyMatter: Published furniture as free instructions and spent his life arguing about who design is actually for.

designers.name: Shiro Kuramata
designers.whyTheyMatter: Made furniture out of expanded steel mesh and acrylic so it looks like it is barely there.

designers.name: Lella Vignelli
designers.whyTheyMatter: Half of a practice usually credited to one name, across furniture, objects and identity.

designers.name: Jasper Morrison
designers.whyTheyMatter: Spent a career removing things from objects until only what is needed is left.

designers.name: Marc Newson
designers.whyTheyMatter: Made compound-curved forms before software made them easy, by beating metal.

designers.name: Fernando and Humberto Campana
designers.whyTheyMatter: Built furniture out of rope, offcuts and stuffed toys, and made it read as luxury rather than poverty.
designers.searchQuery: Fernando and Humberto Campana Furniture design work

designers.name: Naoto Fukasawa
designers.whyTheyMatter: Designs for the behaviour people already have, so the object seems to have been there all along.
designers.searchQuery: Naoto Fukasawa Industrial design design work

designers.name: Hella Jongerius
designers.whyTheyMatter: Treats colour and material as the real design work rather than the finishing stage.

designers.name: Konstantin Grcic
designers.whyTheyMatter: Trained as a cabinetmaker and designs like an engineer arguing with one.

designers.name: Ayşe Birsel
designers.whyTheyMatter: Made her design process explicit and teachable, which most designers never manage.
designers.searchQuery: Ayşe Birsel Industrial design design work

designers.name: Patricia Urquiola
designers.whyTheyMatter: Brings textile and craft techniques into industrial production without making them look nostalgic.

designers.name: Oki Sato (Nendo)
designers.whyTheyMatter: Produces at a volume nobody else attempts, each piece built on one small observation.

designers.name: Bibi Seck
designers.whyTheyMatter: Designs for and manufactures in West Africa, using recycled plastic waste as the input.

designers.name: Jomo Tariku
designers.whyTheyMatter: Draws on Ethiopian objects and forms directly, and has spent years arguing for African design in collections.

designers.name: Nifemi Marcus-Bello
designers.whyTheyMatter: Designs around what Lagos can actually manufacture, and treats that constraint as the brief.
designers.searchQuery: Nifemi Marcus-Bello Industrial design design work

designers.name: Nipa Doshi
designers.whyTheyMatter: Half of Doshi Levien, bringing Indian craft and narrative into European industrial production without flattening either.

designers.name: Nada Debs
designers.whyTheyMatter: Works between Middle Eastern craft inlay and a stripped-back geometry, manufacturing in the region rather than exporting the idea.

designers.name: Aissa Dione
designers.whyTheyMatter: Rebuilt a weaving industry around Senegalese cotton and looms, supplying European houses from Dakar.
